t:
At some unknown time the sorcerer Firez, banished by the surviving June for necromancy, tried to seize the allod of Jigran, bringing with him the power of the Xadagan Empire. He enslaved the June and surrounded the allod with a magical barrier that hid Jigran from everyone, including the curse of the June. But the spells did irreparable damage to the allod. All the strength drained out of the island, the vegetation withered, the animals died out. Firez raised the beasts and, turning them into zombies, put them into his service. Meanwhile the dying land yielded very poor harvests, and the people of Kania could barely hold back the onslaught of Firez's army.

Jigran had long been a province of Kania. Fortresses were built here and farms established. With the coming of Firez and his all-destroying spells the land stopped bearing fruit, and the fortresses turned from settlements into military camps that barely held out against the pressure of the undead. The largest town, Dar Leanos, is the capital of Kanian Jigran. Here stands the portal from Lightwood, and here live Baron Virill and most of the soldiers.

To the south-west lies the fortress of Dar Ulgorn, which has changed hands more than once. Xadagan settlements stretch to the west. In the far west stand two fortresses: the northern one is the stronghold of Firez himself, the southern one serves as a prison for June scholars. There is also a crossing — ruins of what was once either a fortress or a town, now inhabited by Firez's men and the undead. Jigran is an island of war where no one stays on the sidelines, so there is not a single settlement here that is peaceful and takes no part in the war. Kanian villages die out one after another after attacks by the undead, harpies and other creatures. There is only one man who lives apart: Uncle Rad, a seller of sweets and, at the same time, a spy for Baron Virill. His tent stands east of the fortress of Dar Ulgorn.

Kech is an allod that was once Kanian and was later captured by the Empire. Kech was the second allod, after Grok, to be attacked by the combined forces of the orcs and the Xadaganians. In 725 the allod was captured by the Empire, which had to fight on two fronts — here and on the allod of Grok, which the League, in the person of the Kanians and the elves who had concluded a military alliance against the Empire, was trying to win back.

t:
Lightwood is a land of snowy foothills that somewhat resembles medieval Europe. Most of it is covered with wooded mountains; valleys give way to copses, which in turn pass into dense forests. Almost everything around is snow-white.

Lightwood belongs to the Kanian Empire; its territory is very large and its population sparse. Most of Lightwood is covered with wooded mountains. The climate is cold; snow falls early and lies for a long time. There are practically no large towns — even the capital of Lightwood is more of a big village, a cluster of two- and three-storey wooden houses. The other settlements, proudly called towns, look even more like overgrown villages.

The main occupations of the people of Lightwood are logging, hunting, and mining ore and gold. People usually live in small groups and treat strangers with suspicion and hostility. The inhabitants of Lightwood are freedom-loving and independent by nature. At the slightest hint of a threat they take up arms without hesitation and defend their interests without wasting time on inquiries. Lightwood is ruled by a governor sent from the capital, but his power can hardly be called absolute. The provinces enjoy considerable autonomy, which the Council does not curtail without reason. Everything there is decided by the local authorities, so every village has its own ways...

Lumenara is the elven allod of the Great House de Ardeur: a shining beacon in the abyss of the Astral, an amber-lit refuge for all who are eager to change this world. Thanks to Renard, this allod has now received all the latest elven technical inventions, and the power of the Light has made it a truly safe place. Besides the elves, Lumenara is home to a tribe of Aviaks who have become their loyal servants, protectors and helpers. It is also the abode of the lesser House de Gloire.

t:
Manodar is a unique jewel among the allods of the Empire. Discovered at the end of Nezeb's reign, this allod became the granary of the Empire. With its rich black soil and warm, settled weather, the allod capable of producing more than four harvests per year.

Surprisingly, before the start of resettlement, its green plains were rather sparsely populated. The only native inhabitants of the allod are the Waterfolk living in the rivers.

However, there are threats even here - the allod is at a rare intersection of astral currents, which is why it is profitable to build mana stations there.  But the influence of mana stations on nature is still poorly understood.

t:
New Igsh, an allod discovered in the last century, is named that for a reason.  It is very similar to the old Igsh as it's almost an exact copy of it, but there is no Dead Sea here.

The whole allod is covered in endless steppes. It's possible that Igsh and New Igsh were likely part of a single biocenosis, since even their fauna and flora are absolutely identical.

Except New Igsh is much less populated. So it can be an example of what the capital allod was like before Nezebgrad absorbed most of it.

t:
Vechnoslavsk is a land of dense forests and swamps. While of interest to any biologist, this allod is largely impassable.  The existing settlements are located on the coast itself, but the depths of the allod are impenetrable swamps full of monstrous mosquitoes.

The swamps are covered with coniferous forests, and the climate can be described as moderately cool. The fauna is represented by numerous invertebrates, amphibians and reptiles, and animals are represented only by saber-toothed squirrels, bats, and martens. At least this is what we managed to find. More detailed research requires better preparation.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Xadagan is a sad example of a consumer attitude towards nature. Once it was similar in everything to Suslanger: there were oases and a unique desert fauna in its territory.

Now this allod has become a construction site, all water resources have been utilized, and the desert is now covered in quarries and buildings under construction. According to Nefer Ur's plan, the entire allod will eventually be turned into a huge metal city.

If another life once existed there, it has been destroyed.

[Map missing]

It belongs to the Empire and is populated by the Zem: even before the Cataclysm, the land from which the allod formed was the centre of their empire. It is held by one of the Great Mages of the Zem (for a time it was held by Nefer Ur himself). The climate is desert.

t:
Yakhch is a unique land in the sense that it's the only allod that has changed a lot over the years. It was once a typical desert allod, but then the Great Tree was planted there.

It changed the desert - it sucked out excess salt, consolidated the sands, and raised the water level. Mixed forests began to grow on the allod, and a different fauna appeared.

Now it's more of a typical allod from the middle latitudes than the hot desert of the south.

[Map missing]

Yakhch was once an ordinary desert allod, but it was here that the druids came in their time, having decided to try planting a seed of the Great Tree in one of the oases. The Tree changed the landscape of Yakhch profoundly. Where there was desert, mighty forests — a true taiga — now rise. The climate changed too: there is more rain and it is colder overall. Today this land is a source of timber, which the Xadaganians ship to various parts of their state.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

[Map missing]

The Great Mage of this allod was the wise Gramon de Doucer, a disciple of the elven mages of old, second in power only slightly to Skrakan. He united everyone who found themselves on his allod after the Night of Woe into a single, largest House, and revived the tradition of the Great Houses, in which the remaining Eight Great Houses now began to take part. Yoggor itself is a rather unusual place: a majestic forest full of enormous trees. Most of the elves live in their own castles, scattered in great numbers across the allod. Although only elves inhabit this allod, there are also those who can pose a threat to lone travellers — various mindless creatures such as giant spiders and mantises. But everything comes to an end, and a terrible fate befell Yoggor too: an extraordinarily deadly spell that changed the familiar way of life on the allod, darkening it with gloom. After the deadly spell, it changed its name to Nocturne.
f:
The House de Desirae has won several times; its present success is owed to Prince Dakkar, the son of our king. It was Prince Dakkar who restored the prestige of necromancy among the Elves, which led the Conclave to lift the last bans on practising it. After that Ball, however, unpleasant events followed: the House de Doucer, or rather its Head, Armando, acted with extraordinary baseness and brought about the death of the prince's bride, a flagrant violation of the rules of the Great Game. Louis de Desirae seized on this to declare the House de Doucer outlaw and confiscated its home allod, Nocturn.
So the House de Desirae now owns two allods: little Tenebra and vast Nocturn.

t:
Aha! That story caught your interest too?

There used to be an imperial mine of ours there. Hundreds of goblins, under the watchful supervision and loud cursing of foremen, mined valuable strategic raw materials there! Well, there were also some natives who lived in the caves, kobolds and miners, but by special order of the Committee, number... oh, I can't remember, 123\16-BIS I think, all the natives were made honorary citizens of the Empire and obliged to work for the good of the country.

And those rascals didn't want to work! No notion of discipline. No faith in a bright future! Idlers!

They conspired with one very clever goblin — Ghim the Greedy is his name — won the trolls over to their side, and drove out all the foremen, engineers and bookkeepers! Now they've got some sort of monarchy or commune there, with Ghim in charge. He's blocked all the tunnels, raked a pile of gold for himself and sits there chuckling — he's beaten the Empire, if you please, the scoundrel.

But every dog has its day! There are still goblins loyal to the Empire on the island, a squad of Boomer demolitionists. They'll blast a tunnel through any rock! With their help you'll easily reach the lair of that separatist and plunderer of the people's economy, the Greedy one.

Whatever treasure you find is yours. And on behalf of the whole working class give Ghim a severe reprimand entered into his skull. The Empire will not forget you!

Bosses: Wick, Stakh Quickpick, Stonegnawer, Ghim the Greedy.

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Imperial allod; mines are located here.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Aha! So this story caught your interest too? It used to be our Imperial mine. Hundreds of goblins, under the watchful guidance and loud cursing of the foremen, dug up valuable strategic resources there! Well, there were some other natives too, who lived in the caves — kobolds and mountainfolk — but by special order of the Committee number... oh, I don't remember, 123\16-BIS or something, all the natives were made honorary citizens of the Empire and obliged to labor for the good of the country. And those rascals didn't want to work! No notion of discipline whatsoever. No faith in the bright future! Lazybones! They conspired with one terribly clever goblin — Ghim the Greedy, they call him — won the trolls over to their side, and drove out all the foremen, engineers and bookkeepers! Now they have something there that's either a monarchy or a commune, and Ghim is their boss. He caved in all the tunnels, raked up a pile of gold for himself, and sits there chuckling — he has beaten the Empire, you see, the scoundrel. But it's not all cakes and ale for the cat! There are still goblins on the island loyal to the Empire, a squad of bang-bang demolishers. They'll blast a tunnel through any rock! With their help you'll easily reach the lair of that separatist and plunderer of the people's economy, Ghim the Greedy. Whatever treasure you find is yours. And deliver Ghim a stern reprimand, on behalf of the whole working class, with an entry in his skull. The Empire will not forget you!

Bosses: Wick, Stakh Quickpick, Stonegnawer, Ghim the Greedy.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t:
The former inhabitants of Altan Tepek are long dead, but deep within the city abandoned mechanisms keep on working.

Bosses: Frostmount, Jasper Defender, Metztlitotec, Ayateotle.

Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, remnants of June mechanisms and ghosts of the June.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler).

Young adventurers are firmly convinced that where there are June ruins, there are countless treasures. Seasoned heroes have learned that in ruins you can sometimes find a hoard, but more often trouble. And the most experienced know that most ruins hold neither treasures nor monsters: small wonder, since they have been there themselves and have already taken care of both. Is there anything on Altan Tepek? I don't know: the islet is placed very awkwardly, nothing but reefs all around. We sailed all the way round it, looked it over through a spyglass, but found nowhere to land. Still, it's a curious place: it looks like a tropical forest, yet there's snow everywhere, frost-covered palms stick up, and the wind howls over the frozen jungle. I thought I noticed some movement, but I never made out who it was: kobold marauders, maybe, or June undead. What, you want to dig about in the old ruins? Well, if you do manage to land, tell me afterwards who was roaming there and why everything froze!

Bosses: Frostmount, Jasper Defender, Metztlitotec, Ayateotle.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t: It was probably the basis for the Astral Graveyard that was made later, the place we reach right before Kirah... at least visually it is very similar. The quests there were given by a Zem locked inside the body of his Guardian.

[Map missing]

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater and Avilon.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, belongs to followers of Tep.

Story:

Sorbas Logey, a senior laboratory assistant at the ZIT Headquarters, was testing a technology for transferring an essence into mechanisms other than Zem bodies. When the ship of their expedition moored at this island, it was attacked by an Astral Monster. After his death on this island, in accordance with his technology, he moved into the body of his robot, the "Astral Guardian"; and the island holds a huge number of undead (although, because of the gift of Tensess, he ought to have ended up in Purgatory). To help sort this out, one must fight one's way into the depths of the island and kill "Little Skull", an undead draconid, clearing the island of the dead along the way. Since after the draconid's death the assistant still remained in the guardian's body, he asked us to reach the center of the island and try to get to the bottom of it there, for in the guardian's body he is weak and cannot get there himself. At the center of the island there turns out to be a place of power and a Cultist Rhetor; after defeating him we return to the guardian. Sorbas says that this place works on the same principle as Tep's pyramid, but now (apparently after the ritual was interrupted) he can go back to Purgatory again.

Bosses: Little Skull, Cultist Rhetor.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Perhaps you have come across creatures touched by the astral. Under its influence they change, and more often than not they do not change for the better… The Astral Horn is just such a creature. It is a unicorn turned into a dangerous monster. Even reaching it will not be easy, let alone defeating it. But there are a few things I know… Once you find the Astral Horn's island, you will have to hack your way through the astral crystals. Quite literally. You need the Hammer of Pain. You can obtain the hammer itself by defeating Splasher, a dangerous water elemental. Then, fighting the granite trolls, you will win the Shards of Pain. The power hidden within them will let you charge your weapon with magic. That can be done in the June ruins guarded by a cyclops called Stomper. Only once you have that weapon will you be able to break through the magic shield barring the way into the Horn's lair. I do not know what awaits you there. Be ready for anything. All that is known is that the Horn is hard to find — it knows how to hide.

Bosses: Splasher, Stomper, Astral Horn.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Tenebra.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited mostly by trolls and lamias.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Perhaps you have already come across creatures touched by the Astral. Under its influence they change, and more often than not they change for the worse...

The Astral Horn is just such a creature. It is a unicorn turned into a dangerous monster. Even reaching it will not be easy, let alone defeating it. But there is something I do know… Once you find the island of the Astral Horn, you will have to hack your way through the astral crystals. Quite literally. You need the Hammer of Pain. You can obtain the hammer itself by defeating Splasher, a dangerous water elemental. Then, fighting the granite trolls, you will collect Shards of Pain. The power hidden in them will let you charge your weapon with magic. That can be done in the June ruins guarded by a cyclops nicknamed Stomper. And only once you have that weapon will you be able to break through the magic shield barring the way to the Horn's lair. I do not know what awaits you there. Be ready for anything. All that is known is that the Horn is not easy to find: it knows how to hide.

Bosses: Splasher, Stomper, Astral Horn.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Gallery: None :/

t:
It resembles Eljune.

We end up in a camp of Free Traders who want to destroy the lair of the pirates who have settled here. They want to do it by killing their leader and the goblins, so that the rest will kill one another fighting for power. Naturally, we are the ones who do all of it for them. Along the way we also catch fish for an Orc and kill a hydra that roars and keeps a delicate Elf lady awake at night.

[Map missing]

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph and the Dragon Ring.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a pirate lair.

Story:

We arrive at a camp of Free Traders who want to destroy the pirate lair that has settled here. According to their plan, to drive the pirates away one must kill their leader and the goblins, so that the rest will slaughter one another fighting for power. Those who remain the Free Traders can finish off themselves. Naturally, we do all of this for them. Along the way we also catch fish for an Orc and kill a hydra that roars at night and keeps a delicate Elf maiden from sleeping.

Bosses: Hydra, Pirate Ataman.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

Most likely the ship crashed, and the Creature got out of the cage and began to kill.

t:
Even seasoned astral captains shudder on hearing of this allod. A dark and inhospitable place, once the domain of the elves of House de Blizare, today it lies in gloom. Its present masters are demons, which means that a journey to the dark allod will be a real ordeal even for the most desperate travelers.

Bosses: Gryzl, Bonegrinder, Hornbearer, Sparky.

Climate: Wasteland, closest to Yazes Shard.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Demons.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The Black Rock... You'll recognize it the moment you approach the island! A lifeless shard of bare stone, gnawed by demonic fangs. It's simply swarming with demons! As far as I know, the Black Rock is all that remains of the allod of the House de Blizare after the Night of Astral Portals. The House de Blizare suffered enormous losses that night. Almost all their mages died in battle; the Great Mage lost his nerve and prepared to open a portal to Kania, which finally broke the fighting spirit of the defenders. The elves fled, leaving their allod to be torn apart by the demons. However, for some reason I can't understand, the allod turned out to be extraordinarily resistant to the effects of the astral. They say the blood of the elven martyrs who defended their home to the last is the cause... But I don't believe it! Elves are deceitful and selfish creatures who know nothing of heroic self-sacrifice. Although by their standards such a death would surely count as beautiful. In short, the Black Rock is now a piece of land crawling with demons. There are as many of them as fleas on a goblin! So I strongly advise you not even to go near this island. An armada of demons is not the enemy you want to run into in the astral!

Bosses: Gryzl, Bonegrinder, Hornbearer, Sparky.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Countess Yasskul Bathory, once the most beautiful of Hickut's rulers, seized on every chance to regain her lost beauty. Unfortunately, she managed to find an effective means of rejuvenation — using the blood of young girls.

It is said the Blood Countess has taken refuge on one of the astral islands. There she has a whole manor with well-drilled and devoted servants. The horrors and debauchery going on in her domain would drive even a battle-hardened warrior mad. But Bathory chose a picturesque, even pleasant, spot. At first glance you would never guess that some evil could be lurking here.

Bosses: Yaver Nadashti, Rolling Hill, Mechanical Watchman, Yasskul Bathory.

Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by the Zem.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The Blood Countess... She who bathes in the blood of young girls to preserve her own beauty... Do you really want to hear this story? I'll tell you straight: it's disgusting. The Blood Countess's real name is Yasskul Bathory. I knew her personally — a pleasant lady and an outstanding researcher. But she had a thing about her appearance. Bathory, once the most beautiful of the rulers of Hickut, seized on any chance to regain her lost beauty. And, unfortunately, she found one... Thanks to her knowledge of ancient blood magic she was able to rejuvenate her body... and kill her soul! Hundreds of ruined women, rivers of blood steeped in terrible spells — that was the price. Bathory was outlawed and sentenced to death, but she managed to escape! Rumor has it that the Blood Countess took refuge on one of the astral islands. She has a whole estate there, with well-drilled and devoted servants. The horrors and debauchery that go on there would drive even a battle-hardened warrior mad! Beware the Blood Countess, if you don't want to become one of her slaves and end your life as a bloodless body on a laboratory floor.

Bosses: Yaver Nadashti, Rolling Hill, Mechanical Watchman, Yasskul Bathory.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Addendum: During internal testing of the island, an amusing bug appeared on it: a pigeon grew to the size of a boss. In the end it was decided to immortalize it and make it a mascot named Gosha. Now it can be met in various places across Sarnaut.

t:
Aha, I know that place. A gloomy little spot, I must say. Once there was a circus there, the most ordinary circus, with clowns, acrobats and a trained bear with a balalaika. But the place wasn't popular. Who would fly through the perilous Astral just to look at some jesters? And so the circus fell into complete ruin.

And then three men turned up there, calling themselves professors, specialists in dreams and fantasies. They patched up the old circus buildings and sent invitations to their Carnival to anyone who wanted one. The masters of the Carnival guarantee the fulfillment of the most secret desires, the most rosy dreams and the most incredible fantasies.

If you ask me, they're charlatans through and through. They don't take money from anyone, by the way, which is really strange. Now, if they wanted to line their pockets, the point of such promises would at least be clear. For now, all I can advise you is — keep your wits about you!

Bosses: Dread, Heat, Red Beard, Harlequin.

Climate: Temperate, cursed land.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by merchants and a circus troupe.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Ah, I know that place. A rather gloomy little place, I must say. Once there was a circus there, a perfectly ordinary circus, with clowns, acrobats and a trained bear with a balalaika. But the place was not popular. Who would fly through the danger-filled Astral just to look at some jesters? And so the circus fell into complete neglect. And then three men turned up there, calling themselves professors, specialists in dreams and fantasies. They patched up the old circus buildings and sent invitations to their Carnival to anyone who wished to come. The masters of the Carnival guarantee the fulfilment of the most cherished desires, the rosiest dreams and the most incredible fantasies. As far as I'm concerned, they are all charlatans, every last one. They don't take money from anyone, by the way, which is very strange. Now if they wanted to line their pockets, then the point of such promises would at least be understandable. For now all I can advise you is — keep your ears pricked!

Bosses: Dread, Heat, Red Beard, Harlequin.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t:
During one of my expeditions I... hmm... had the misfortune to visit the island of the Catacombs. On my first visit it was a deserted place, keeping the peace of one of Tep's Pyramids.

My second visit was clear confirmation of the sad fact that the cult of Tep has been restored. Now his followers are in charge of the Catacombs. They are using stone elementals to dig out the Pyramid. I don't know what they are looking for there — my companions and I, many of whom were seriously wounded in the fight, had to leave the island in haste. I am sure nothing good can come of the activities of Tep's followers. I ask you to find this island and put an end to the cultists' doings. You will have to fight both them and their stone elementals. And above all, destroy Isdes, the high priest of Tep, who is directing the excavation of the Pyramid.

Bosses: Variant 1: Tep's Prelate, Tailstabber, Isdes. Variant 2: Longbelly, Tep's Prelate, Isdes, Sefnut.

Climate: Desert, closest to the Den.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Tep's cultists.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

During one of my expeditions I was... hm... unlucky enough to visit the Tomb Isle. On my first visit it was a deserted place keeping the peace of one of Tep's Pyramids. My second visit was a vivid confirmation of the sad fact that Tep's cult has been restored. Now his followers rule the Tomb. They use stone elementals to dig out the Pyramid. I do not know what they are looking for there — my companions and I, many of whom were seriously wounded in the fight, had to leave the island in a hurry. I am sure nothing good can be expected from the activities of Tep's followers. I ask you to find that island and put an end to the cultists' doings. You will have to fight both them and their stone elementals. And most importantly — destroy Isdes, Tep's high priest, who leads the excavation of the Pyramid.

Bosses: Variant 1: Tep's Prelate, Tailstabber, Isdes. Variant 2: Longbelly, Tep's Prelate, Isdes, Sefnut.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t:
Do you hear the roar of the crowd? The spectators want to see new heroes! Cowards, weaklings and pacifists had better keep away from this place! Everyone else will find on the island of the Den wealth, entertainment and the love of a gambling crowd. You will have a chance to meet the most famous smugglers, mercenaries and slave traders. And the master of the allod is so fond of cruel entertainments that he holds gladiatorial fights every day.

Fight other daredevils in the arena to win fabulous treasures. Like true gladiators, you are not obliged to kill defeated enemies — perhaps some of them deserve mercy. The crowd craves only one thing: the ring of steel and hot blood spilling onto the sand!

Bosses: Mussle, Spartacus, Cerbarath, Caligula.

Climate: Desert, closest to the Catacombs.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by smugglers and the like.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Thanks be to Yasker, the Empire has no shortage of places for cultured recreation. If you like, go to the cinema; if you like, to a museum or a library; if you like, take a trip to a sanatorium, or to the Summer Atoll. Not enough excitement in your life — then play the sports lottery! And yet even here we still have elements for whom such entertainments are not enough; they want something hotter and more forbidden. And this in the Empire — as for the debauchery that goes on abroad, I simply keep silent! Well, as long as there is demand, there will be supply. In short, one crafty goblin found a stable islet in the Astral and set up an arena for gladiatorial fights there. Almost like on Yazes — only without demons, but with gambling and young ladies of dubious reputation. What riff-raff does not hang about there: mercenaries, and smugglers, and slave traders... They drink, place bets, cut each other for nothing. Shame and disgrace! Decent people have no business there, mark my words.

Bosses: Mussle, Spartacus, Cerbarath, Caligula.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.
f: Based on the Shard of Umoir.

t:
A passion for destruction is an extremely dangerous passion. The consequences can be especially tragic if the desire to destroy everything flares up in the heart of an outstanding person. You can see this once again on the allod of Cinderland — once a luxurious hunting preserve of the Empire.

Of the former grandeur and beauty of this place only the charred skeletons of huge trees remain as a reminder. Fire has swallowed the whole island, turning the allod into a living monument to the terrible experiments of a Great Mage.

Bosses: Kuzmich, Oakwarden, Volkh, Fireborn.

Climate: Temperate, closest to the Igsh Military District.

Affiliation: Imperial allod, the site of a hunting estate.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The Cinderland... Yes, there's no other name for that islet now. And yet once it was the finest hunting reserve in the Empire! They say the Great Yasker himself liked to shoot ducks or run down a deer in that reserve. And the local forester, Kuzmich, was a fine drinking companion — sometimes we'd get so plastered with him that in the morning we forgot which of us was the forester and which the traveler. Hm, those were the days... And now there's nothing there but charred trunks sticking up and rabid beasts running about. Curse that mad Arisen Zem! And at first they received him as an honored guest. Why, an outstanding scholar had decided to pursue his research in the quiet of the forest! They arranged every comfort for him, you understand — a laboratory in the woods, peace and bliss. He worked away, clinking his flasks... But Kuzmich, kind soul, decided to find himself a drinking companion. He could hardly drink with the bears, after all? And he took to dropping in on this mage, to chat about science over a bottle or two. And Kuzmich's hooch is mighty strong! Kuzmich was fine, he has a cast-iron throat and a steel liver, but the wizard, blast him, drank himself into the horrors. And in his drunken state he went completely off his rocker, foundations and all. The swine set the forest on fire! He imagined himself the Fireborn, the Great Fire Mage, lord of flame, anchor up his stern! And that was it, the reserve was done for — for he really is a Great mage, so now the forest there burns but does not burn up, the animals blaze but do not roast, and the most terrible thing is that the spirit of the forest, old Oakwarden, fell under his spell and serves him. And Kuzmich has taken to drinking out of grief; he recognizes no one, just swills vodka without ever sobering up. I tried to bring him to his senses, but he punched me in the face and kicked me out of his hut, where a pack of fire wolves was already waiting. They chased me all the way to my ship and burnt such a hole in my trousers — it's a shame to say. At least they didn't singe my hide. So if you mean to pay a visit to the Cinderland that is left of the reserve, don't forget to take a fire extinguisher with you — believe me, it's blazing there good and proper.

Bosses: Kuzmich, Oakwarden, Volkh, Fireborn.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t:
I know that place. Only I strongly advise you not to fly there!

On that island there's a whole village of religious fanatics. Unwashed peasants, who until recently were meekly growing turnips for the Kanian soldiery, have got above themselves. They've renounced faith in the Light, not to mention veneration of the saints Nezeb and Skrakan, and worship some kind of nature spirits. And in charge of them is the volkhv Jaromir. It was he, that bearded lunatic, who stirred all the peasants to revolt! He's completely addled the village men's heads with his tales about the faith of their ancestors, the greatness of ancient Kania, glorious Traditions... No, honoring traditions is sacred. But with some sense! We're building mana stations and underground metros, the League is treading on our heels in industrial development, and they're still living in the last millennium. A wild people, in a word — not like us, the enlightened citizens of the great Empire.

So if the road leads you to Clear Mountain, get ready to fight the whole village at once. And the local bogatyrs as well — Alexei, Ivan and Vladislav, great hulking brutes: step out of line and they'll pound you into the ground up to your ears. But if you manage to defeat Jaromir himself, maybe the peasants will come to their senses and stop grabbing every stranger and throwing him into the Astral...

Bosses: Aunt Agafya, Vladislav the Cruel, Prokopy, Jaromir.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Lightwood.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a Kanian settlement.

t: Until recently this rich mine belonged to Umoir merchants. That is, they thought it belonged to them — but in fact the Mistress lives in the depths of the island to this day. If she wants, she shares her riches; if she doesn't, she sends misfortune. And so she stopped wanting to. Whether people angered her with their greed or failed to show her respect, but now wolves and bears roam the village instead of miners. I wouldn't fly there: what if the Mistress gets angry with me too! Her riches in the depths are, of course, countless — only she guards them so well that you can't get near them!

Bosses: Fire Jumper, Blue Yaga, Mighty Poloz, Mistress of the Copper Mountain.

Climate: Temperate, closest to Avilon.

Affiliation: League allod, inhabited by Kanians.

Astral island:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Story allod:

For a ritual Velerad needed living gems — prophetic yakhonts, which could be found only on the island of Copper Mountain. It turned out that the island had once belonged to Goldie Nickel, but Goldie had lost it, and the new owner was his brother Zavid Nickel, a greedy, grasping man. Meanwhile disaster had struck the workings: something was frightening the miners to death, and they refused to work. The heroes tried to get to the bottom of it, and they had to pass a difficult path of riddles and trials to reach the local Sovereign — the Mistress of the Local Mountain. She punished Zavid for his greed by turning him to stone, but agreed to give a yakhont on condition that the mine be returned to Goldie and the way to her underground halls be forgotten. Alas, if anything in the world is immortal, it is human greed. Learning of the halls of the Mistress of the Copper Mountain, which were full of precious stones, people fitted out more than one expedition, breaking the agreement. After the ritual Velerad never learned where the Plague had come from. The visions were hazy and incomprehensible.

Bosses: Fire Jumper, Blue Yaga, Mighty Poloz, Mistress of the Copper Mountain.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Umoir Archipelago. Story allod.

Addendum: The island was made on the basis of concepts by a player nicknamed Merani. The Servant of Light on the allod is a reference to her.

t:
In places it resembles a snowbound Eljune.

We meet an Aviak Elder, who tells us that this island has been cursed for a hundred years. The Aviaks guard this place from wanderers so that their deaths do not strengthen the unclean creatures, and so that the curse does not creep out into the outside world. We try to defeat the nearest creatures and somehow manage. The Elder tells us that there is, you see, a Spirit here that helps them in this task, and since we are stronger than the Aviaks, we might ask the spirit and perhaps defeat the curse.

The Spirit tells us that long ago a strange shadow flew in from the distant astral but stopped here, by the church. And it began spreading its corruption: the people abandoned this place, the land rotted, the animals were twisted. So the spirit stayed behind to fight the curse. He sends us to the south-west of the island to find and destroy the source of the corruption. It turns out to be the Dark Side of Tensess.

[Map missing]

Climate: Taiga, closest to Eljune.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, formerly Kanian.

Story:

We are met by the Aviak Elder. He tells us that they (the aviaks) have been guarding this place for a very long time, so that the evil does not get out and so that the strangers who come to this island do not feed the EVIL with strength. The aviak suggests that we go to the guarded borders and see from whom they are protecting the world. We discover banshees and decide they ought to be killed. Besides the ordinary ones, we also defeat an ancient banshee and return. The aviak is amazed at our courage and strength and says that the banshees are apparently scouts, but the shadows by the second bridge are already closer to the source. If you manage to defeat them too, find the spirit of the priest in one of the huts.

We head there, defeat the Shadows and look for the hut with the priest. The Hermit Spirit (the priest) tells us that in the times of the great battles he felt some shadow flying from the depths of the astral, but it could not fly any further. It stopped near our church. That is when it all began: the earth began to rot, the animals changed horribly, shadows began to crawl out. The Kanians left these places, but he, a servant of Tensess, decided to stay, and tried to cleanse these places and drive out the shadows. By his reckoning, his attempts to cope with the evil only helped it to spread.

In his helplessness the aviaks began to help him. He points out to us that the source of the evil lies beyond the church, to the southeast. Arriving at the spot, we discover that the cause of the horrors on this island is a part — the evil part — of the soul of Tensess. And we destroy it.

Bosses: Ancient Banshee, Ancient Shadow, the Dark Side of Tensess.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.
